title: rest: a batch, updateMany or deleteMany whose rows failed answers HTTP 200 with success:false; answer 207 so a raw client can tell
body:
domain:server#2 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufziCTpjnYbdh76SAWwb

Filing gate: ④ per-layer child of #32169 (p2, filed on the maintainer's 「立卡处理」 after the 2026-11-10 platform test run #32135). Split by the seat on the card thread's phase-1 report, measured on a live showcase at `origin/main` `bb472154` (report: `/mnt/project-files/server-orders/seat2/32169-phase1-report.md`, project files).
Reader: the next `domain:server` seat that claims it.

## What happens

`POST /data/:object/batch` (update/delete/create, `atomic` or not), `/updateMany` and `/deleteMany` answer **200** `{success:false, total, succeeded:0, failed:N, results:[…]}` when every row failed (`packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts`, ~L503 and the many-handlers). `createMany` with a bad row answers **400** for the whole call, so the bulk family disagrees with itself.

The SDK's shared `fetch` throws on any non-2xx (`packages/client/src/index.ts` ~L8309), and the console's `updateMany`/`deleteMany` ride it, so a 4xx would turn today's per-row `results` into a thrown error.

## Expected

Answer **207 Multi-Status** with the body unchanged when rows failed (seat's reading: when `failed > 0`; the claiming seat confirms or narrows to `succeeded === 0`). 207 keeps `res.ok` true, so the SDK and console keep working, and a raw HTTP client can branch on it.

Clause-②: yes (narrowing): a changed status a client could branch on. BREAKING obligations apply (`!` title, banner, ADR-0087 disposition, dogfood battery). Metadata-protocol: none.
Business reason: integrations that read only the HTTP status today count an all-failed batch as success.
